messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a spike in fallback hits this morning for tenant=acme when their p50 CPU spiked. Can we align on an ordering and a sensible header-override rule? :thinking:
ben: saw that too. looks like gateway matched the route, then header `X-Model-Variant` forced a variant that didn't have capacity -> cb tripped -> backup model. we need clearer precedence.
anna: suggestion: route match > tenant quota check > header override only if `allow-header-override=true` on the route config. else ignore header and fall through to normal priority. small and explicit.
thomas: agree. Also add a metric tag `fallback_reason` so we know if it was `header_override`, `cb_open`, or `quota_shed`. Telemetry currently only records `fallback=true`.
maria: +1 on the metric. can we also return an explicit header in responses when fallback happens, e.g. `X-Redwood-Fallback: cb_open;model=m-small` so clients can degrade gracefully?
ben: yes. That'll help users show an inline banner instead of failing. We should standardize values: `X-Redwood-Fallback: <reason>;model=<name>;route=<route-id>`
anna: small config prototype I hacked:```yaml
routes:
  - id: text-gen
    match: "/v1/generate"
    allow_header_override: false
    fallback_chain:
      - id: model-x-large
        priority: primary
      - id: model-x-small
        priority: backup
    circuit_breaker:
      error_rate: 0.2
      min_requests: 50
```
thomas: looks good. two additions: 1) circuit breaker should track sustained latency spikes not just error rate (latency percentile) 2) we should allow per-tenant override for urgent enterprise customers (but gated behind dedicated capacity flag).
maria: for the console UX, can we visualize the chain and simulation mode? e.g., a toggle to simulate a cb_open and show expected routing and cost delta. product asked for that in last roadmap.
ben: yes — console should show: chain order, matching precedence, estimated qps, historical fallback_count and latency delta. add a 'preview' button that runs a dry-run against selected tenants.
anna: dry-run needs to simulate crowding/kv cache misses too, otherwise the results will be optimistic. we should surface `simulated_kv_miss_rate` and `simulated_batch_size` in preview results.
maria: operational ask: add an alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m for top routes. also notify SE when tenant-level fallback spikes.
thomas: cc @deploy-bot — can you add a flag to rollout so we can flip `allow_header_override` per route in a canary first? we want 5% traffic then 25% then 100%.
deploy-bot: automated-note: rollout plan created for route "text-gen". stages: 5%,25%,100%. CI checks: config lint, policy-checks, telemetry hooks.
ben: follow-up: we need to document behavior when both header override and tenant routing hint exist. propose: tenant hint > route-level header > global default. call it 'hint precedence' and publish in API docs.
maria: okay let's do action items: 1) anna: PR with config schema + default precedence (ETA EOD) 2) thomas: telemetry change (fallback_reason + latency_delta) + alerts (ETA tomorrow) 3) ben: console preview mockups (ETA next week) 4) i'll owner rollout plan and doc (ETA EOW).
anna: working on PR now. will add tests for preview simulation and a unit test for ignoring header when `allow_header_override=false`.
thomas: I'll add latency-based cb to the runtime and a metric for sustained percentile breaches.
maria: thanks all. good call. :rocket:
